pain_points.text: Requisitions arrive incomplete, which causes back-and-forth before a PO can be raised.
pain_points.impact: Rework for procurement; slower cycle time for requesters.

pain_points.text: Approval routing depends on people knowing who to email.
pain_points.impact: Approvals stall or go to the wrong person; no reliable record of who approved what.

pain_points.text: Supplier onboarding documents are collected inconsistently.
pain_points.impact: POs can be issued to suppliers whose due diligence (KYC) is incomplete: a regulatory risk.

pain_points.text: Three-way match (PO, goods receipt, invoice) is checked by hand.
pain_points.impact: Payment delays, late-payment friction with suppliers, and errors that are hard to trace.

stakeholders: Fast, simple way to buy what they need
Fair sourcing, controlled spend, less rework
Invoices match POs and receipts; budget control
Manage closely; own approval matrix and tolerances
Full audit trail, supplier due diligence (KYC)

requirements.text: Every purchase must be traceable from request to payment, including who approved it and when.
No purchase order may be issued to a supplier whose due diligence is not verified.
Invoices that match the PO and goods receipt within tolerance are paid without manual checking.
The requisition form enforces mandatory fields (item description, quantity, estimated value, cost centre, budget code, need-by date, spend category) and blocks submission until they are complete.
After a cost centre is selected, only budget codes valid for that cost centre are offered.
The system routes each requisition to approvers using the approval matrix (value threshold and spend category).
Approvers see remaining budget for the cost centre alongside the request value.
Approval requests not actioned within 2 working days are escalated to the approver's delegate.
Supplier status (Pending, Verified, Expired, Blocked) is held on the supplier record; a PO cannot be issued unless status is Verified.
Supplier onboarding uses a standard document checklist; compliance is notified 30 days before any document expires.
Requesters confirm goods or service receipt in the system against the PO.
The system matches invoice, PO and goods receipt on quantity and price; matches within tolerance are marked ready for payment, mismatches go to an exception queue with the reason.
Requesters can see the status of their requisition at each stage.
A monthly report shows cycle time, first-time-complete rate, match rate and spend with unverified suppliers.
Every create, approve, reject, change and payment action is logged with user, timestamp and before/after values; the log cannot be edited.
Role-based access; segregation of duties so the same person cannot raise and approve a requisition, or create a supplier and approve a payment to it.
Audit records are retained for the period required by the bank's record-retention policy.

rules: Up to ₦1m: line manager. ₦1m–₦10m: line manager + budget holder. Over ₦10m: + Head of Procurement and Finance Director.
IT hardware/software also needs IT approval; legal or consultancy services also need Legal approval, at any value.
Match tolerance (to be agreed with Finance)
Price: ±2% per line. Quantity: no over-receipt; under-receipt is matched to the quantity received.
Only Verified suppliers can receive POs. Status becomes Expired automatically when a mandatory document passes its expiry date.
The requester cannot approve their own requisition. Whoever creates a supplier cannot approve payments to that supplier.

stories.want: a guided requisition form with mandatory fields and budget codes
stories.so: I do not have to resubmit my request
ac: Given a required field is empty, when I try to submit, then the form blocks submission and highlights the field.
Given I have selected a cost centre, then only budget codes valid for that cost centre are shown.

stories.want: requisitions to route to the right approver automatically by value threshold and category
stories.so: I no longer chase approvals by email
ac: Given a requisition exceeds an approval threshold, when it is approved at one level, then it routes to the next level automatically.
Every approval records the approver, timestamp and decision.

stories.want: the system to block POs to any supplier whose due diligence documents are not verified
stories.so: we never pay an unvetted supplier
ac: Given a supplier's status is Pending, when a PO is raised for that supplier, then the system blocks it and shows which documents are missing.

stories.want: invoices matched automatically to POs and goods receipts
ac: Given the invoice, PO and receipt match within tolerance, then the invoice is marked ready for payment.
Given a mismatch, then the invoice goes to the exception queue with the reason.

stories.want: a standard onboarding checklist and alerts before documents expire
stories.so: supplier files stay complete without manual tracking
ac: Given a new supplier, then all checklist documents must be uploaded before status can be set to Verified.
Given a document expires in 30 days, then compliance receives a notification.

stories.want: to see remaining budget next to each request
stories.so: I can decide without asking finance
ac: Given a requisition assigned to me, when I open it, then I see the cost centre, budget remaining and request value.
Given approving would exceed budget, then I must enter a reason to approve.

stories.want: a complete, uneditable history of each purchase
stories.so: I can evidence controls without rebuilding email trails
ac: Given any requisition, PO or invoice, then I can view every action with user, timestamp and before/after values.
No user, including administrators, can edit or delete audit entries.

stories.so: my request does not wait while an approver is away
ac: Given an approval has not been actioned for 2 working days, then it is sent to the approver's delegate and the requester is notified.

stories.want: to confirm receipt of goods against the PO in the system
stories.so: finance can match and pay the invoice
ac: Given goods arrive, when I record the received quantity against the PO, then a goods receipt is created and linked to the PO.

stories.want: to see where my requisition is
stories.so: I do not have to email procurement for updates
ac: Given I open my requisitions, then each shows its current stage and who it is waiting on.

stories.want: a monthly report of P2P performance
stories.so: I can show the process is under control
ac: The report shows requisition-to-PO cycle time, first-time-complete rate, first-time match rate and spend with unverified suppliers (which must be zero).

stories.want: segregation of duties enforced by the system
stories.so: no single person can complete a purchase alone
ac: Given I raised a requisition, then I cannot approve it.
Given I created a supplier, then I cannot approve payments to that supplier.

kpis: Median working days from requisition submitted to PO issued
Reduce (baseline to be measured in discovery)
Requisitions approved without being returned for missing information ÷ all requisitions
PO value issued to suppliers not in Verified status
Invoices matched within tolerance without manual intervention ÷ all invoices
Median days from invoice receipt to payment
Internal audit findings raised against the P2P process
